name: NC IDEA SEED Grant
amount_text: $50,000, paid in milestone tranches over 6 to 12 months, plus mentorship
deadline_text: Twice a year (spring and fall). Spring 2027: opens Jan 25, closes Feb 22, 5:00pm
requirements: Headquartered in NC with most operations in NC for 12 months after grant
At least one full-time founder lives in NC
Revenue-generating or on a path to revenue; over $250K trailing revenue less likely to be selected
Over $250K equity raised or over $1M in grants less likely to be selected
Must be state-registered with a federal EIN
Apply to SEED or MICRO in a cycle, not both
Not for local service businesses, consulting or training firms, distributors, franchises, resellers or nonprofits
notes: Competitive startup grant; 130 to 180 applicants per cycle and usually 5 to 7 winners.

name: NC IDEA MICRO Grant
amount_text: $10,000 (75% at signing, 25% about two months later) plus an 8-week customer discovery program
deadline_text: Twice a year. Spring 2027: opens Jan 25, closes Feb 22, 5:00pm
requirements: Headquartered in NC; at least one founder lives in NC
Founder full-time within 6 to 12 months of applying
Already active (customer discovery, prototype, or early revenue); expect revenue within 12 months
Food and beverage companies need at least $5,000 annual revenue
High-capital, long-runway companies such as pharma are not eligible
notes: Smaller, earlier-stage version of SEED; regional info sessions include Winston-Salem/Triad.

name: One North Carolina Small Business Program: Incentive Funds
funder: NC Department of Commerce, Office of Science, Technology & Innovation (for NC Board of Science, Technology & Innovation)
amount_text: Reimburses part of the cost of preparing a federal Phase I SBIR/STTR proposal; about $210,000 total available for FY2027; per-award cap not stated on page (check site)
deadline_text: Accepted until June 30, 2027 or until funds run out
requirements: Technology-based small business based in North Carolina
Must be preparing or have submitted a federal Phase I SBIR/STTR proposal
See FY2027 solicitation for full criteria
notes: Helps cover proposal-writing costs for a first federal SBIR/STTR attempt; apply through CyberGrants.

name: One North Carolina Small Business Program: SBIR/STTR Matching Funds
funder: NC Department of Commerce, Office of Science, Technology & Innovation
amount_text: State match for companies holding a federal Phase I SBIR/STTR award; about $1.92M total for FY2027, plus a $25,000 add-on for Hurricane Helene-impacted areas; per-award cap not stated on page (check site)
deadline_text: FY2027 Matching solicitation released Dec 14, 2026; accepted until June 30, 2027 or until funds run out
requirements: NC technology-based small business
Must already hold a federal Phase I SBIR or STTR award
See FY2027 solicitation for full criteria
notes: Bridges the gap between federal Phase I and Phase II; only useful after winning a federal SBIR/STTR award.

name: Golden LEAF Open Grants Program
deadline_text: Rolling with bimonthly board review. Next Stage 1 deadlines: Dec 24, 2026; Feb 18, 2027; Apr 22, 2027 (12 PM)
requirements: 501(c)(3) nonprofits and government entities only; for-profits not listed as eligible
Project must fit job creation, workforce preparedness, agriculture, or community competitiveness
Two-stage application; Stage 2 needs prior-year audits and financials
Declined projects cannot resubmit for six months
notes: Big statewide economic development funder; a business would partner with a county, town, college, or nonprofit.

name: NC Building Reuse Program
funder: NC Department of Commerce, Rural Economic Development Division / Rural Infrastructure Authority
region: North Carolina (Tier 1 and 2 counties and rural census tracts in Tier 3 counties)
amount_text: Recent awards $50,000 to $500,000 to local governments
deadline_text: Periodic rounds reviewed by the Rural Infrastructure Authority; check site
requirements: Local government applies on behalf of the business
Building must be vacant, or occupied by an existing NC company that is renovating or expanding
Tied to job creation commitments
Forsyth is not Tier 1/2, so only rural Tier 3 census tracts qualify
notes: Businesses benefit indirectly through their town or county; Oct 2026 round funded 6 Building Reuse projects.

name: NC Passport to Export STEP (State Trade Expansion Program)
funder: Economic Development Partnership of North Carolina (SBA STEP funds)
amount_text: Reimbursement up to $12,000 (up to $3,000 trade show travel; up to $8,000 for booth, export services, website localization, EXIM fees, etc.)
deadline_text: STEP 13 runs June 30, 2026 to Sept 29, 2027; no application deadline posted, contact program manager
requirements: 500 or fewer employees
Registered to do business in NC
In business at least one year
Profitable based on US operations
Products or services with at least 51% US content
Not debarred from federal business
notes: Real grant money for exporters; special consideration for women-, minority-, veteran-owned, and rural businesses.

name: NC Job Ready Grants (Workforce Investment Grants)
funder: NC Department of Commerce, Division of Workforce Solutions via local Workforce Development Boards
amount_text: No dollar figures on page; depends on new hires, county tier, and capital investment
deadline_text: No deadlines posted; check site
requirements: Local Workforce Development Board applies for the employer
For businesses locating or expanding in NC as part of an economic development project
Can fund on-the-job training and incumbent worker training
notes: Contact NCWorks Business Services (800-562-6333) or your local board; tied to expansion projects.

name: Mobile Sources Emissions Reductions Grant (MSERG)
funder: NC Department of Environmental Quality, Division of Air Quality (EPA DERA funds, may add VW Mitigation funds)
amount_text: About $1.09M was available in the 2024 cycle; cost share set by EPA DERA rules (check DERA Eligibility Tool)
deadline_text: 2024 cycle closed Jan 31, 2025 (awards Oct 1, 2025); next cycle not posted, check site or join listserv
requirements: Any private or public entity with a physical presence in NC
Replace, repower, or convert older diesel trucks and equipment
Old equipment must have run within the past two years
Replacement must operate at least 70% in NC for five years
notes: One of the few grants a private trucking fleet can apply for directly; old truck must be scrapped.

name: NC AgVentures Farm Grant
funder: NC Cooperative Extension (NC State) with NC Tobacco Trust Fund Commission
region: North Carolina (listed counties incl. Forsyth and Guilford)
amount_text: Up to $10,000; about 190 farmer grants and 10 community grants
deadline_text: Opens Oct 15, 2026; closes Dec 15, 2026 at 6pm or when 200 applications are received
requirements: Farm must have at least one year of revenue
Farm in an eligible county
One application per farm per year
Total project budget at least 15% above the request
Finish project in 12 months; carry insurance; file two reports
Contact your Extension agent by Dec 1
notes: Good fit for small farms adding a new enterprise; portal caps at 200 applications so apply early.

name: Community Rehabilitation Program Partnership (Supported Employment / Work Adjustment)
funder: NC DHHS Division of Employment and Independence for People with Disabilities (formerly Vocational Rehabilitation)
amount_text: Reimbursement contract (milestone or performance-based rates), not a lump-sum grant
deadline_text: Last formal RFA (RACRP 1059) was issued Apr 30, 2024; applications considered on an ongoing basis for future award dates; check site
requirements: Public or private, nonprofit or for-profit Community Rehabilitation Program
CARF, COA, or CQL accreditation in employment services (or evidence of application)
NC business registration and criminal background check policy
SAM registration and federal exclusion certification
Proof of insurance
notes: Main state funding route for nonprofits doing job placement for people with disabilities; paid per milestone.

name: Incumbent Worker Training and On-the-Job Training (WIOA)
funder: Piedmont Triad Regional Council Workforce Development Board (NCWorks)
region: Alamance, Caswell, Davie, Davidson, Forsyth, Randolph, Rockingham, Stokes, Surry, Yadkin counties, NC
amount_text: Amounts set by the local board; state rules require employer match of 10% (up to 50 employees), 25% (51 to 100), 50% (over 100)
deadline_text: Rolling; contact Business Services team
requirements: Employer current on all taxes
Operating in NC 12 or more months
Trainees are W-2 employees (IWT) or new hires (OJT)
Cannot use IWT to train new hires
Employer must cover the non-federal match
notes: Federal WIOA money that pays part of training costs for your staff; Forsyth employers go through PTRC.

name: Winston-Salem Foundation Community Grants: Small Grants
amount_text: Up to $2,000 ($500 cap for youth athletic teams)
deadline_text: Winter 2026 cycle closed Feb 16; Summer 2026 cycle cancelled; program to relaunch in 2027, check site
requirements: Charitable organizations and groups serving Forsyth County
Annual income of $150,000 or less
No individuals, for-profits, or start-up/operating costs
Project must end after funding decision
notes: Entry-level grant for very small community groups; does not need to be a large nonprofit.

name: Winston-Salem Foundation Capacity-Building Grants
deadline_text: No deadline listed; check site
requirements: Nonprofits serving Forsyth County
Categories: governance/leadership, learning/evaluation, technical skills, diversity/equity/inclusion
notes: Funds strengthening the organization itself (training, systems, evaluation), not programs.

name: Women's Fund of Winston-Salem Grants
deadline_text: Annual; 2026 window was May 4 to June 15; check site for 2027
requirements: Organizations building economic security for women and girls in Forsyth County
notes: Nonprofit grant for programs aimed at women's and girls' economic security.

name: BPI Building an Inclusive Economy Grants
amount_text: Amount not listed (check site)
deadline_text: Annual; 2026 window was Mar 30 to May 4; check site for 2027
requirements: Organizations building economic security for Black households in Forsyth County
notes: For nonprofits (not businesses) doing Black wealth-building, small business support, and similar work.

name: Civic Engagement & Inclusion: Community-Led Organizations
deadline_text: Annual; 2026 window May 1 to June 12 (extended); decisions mid-September
requirements: Organizations or fiscally sponsored groups led by impacted communities
Prioritizes fewer than 5 full-time staff, 10 years or less operating, budget up to $500,000
Priority to Latine-led and immigrant-serving organizations
One Civic Engagement or Housing grant per cycle
notes: Good fit for young grassroots groups; fiscal sponsorship appears acceptable (confirm with staff).

name: Winston-Salem Foundation Animal Welfare Grants
deadline_text: Open Nov 16, 2026 to Jan 5, 2027
requirements: Nonprofits serving animals in Forsyth County
notes: Currently open; narrow focus on animal welfare nonprofits.

name: Forsyth County Community Grants
amount_text: FY27 awards ranged $2,500 to $376,000 ($1.77M total); funding subject to Board approval
deadline_text: FY28 window anticipated Jan 15 to Feb 15, 2027 (per county page); FY27 closed Nov 30, 2025
requirements: Nonprofit agencies offering services to county residents
Must align with county goals: safety, health, education, cultural, economic opportunity
Apply through the Community Portal
One-year grant term, July 1 to June 30
notes: County general fund grants to local nonprofits; watch for the January 2027 window.

name: Forsyth County Small Business Individual Development Account (IDA)
funder: Forsyth County Community & Economic Development (with Experiment in Self Reliance and S.G. Atkins CDC)
amount_text: Matched savings; match rate not stated (program reports $35K owner savings matched with $136K)
deadline_text: Applications closed for 2025 cohort; next cohort not posted, check site
requirements: Existing small business at least one year old
Owner income below 120% of Forsyth County AMI
Save $100 to $200 per month and submit monthly budgets
Attend monthly financial literacy classes and small business courses; meet with coach
notes: Not a direct grant: the county matches money you save for business use. Contact the program to ask about the next cohort.

name: City of Winston-Salem Small Business Plan Contest
funder: City of Winston-Salem, Business Inclusion and Advancement
amount_text: $5,000 grant for each of two winners, plus a potential $5,000 matching micro-loan
deadline_text: Annual; 2026 contest proposals were due Mar 23, 2026, winners announced in fall; check site for 2027
requirements: For-profit micro-business with 5 or fewer employees
Located in the NRSA
Must create low- to moderate-income jobs or benefit that community
2-page proposal, then full business plan for finalists
notes: Small but local; check your address against the NRSA map first.

name: Community Foundation of Greater Greensboro Grants and Initiatives
amount_text: Up to $25,000 (2025 cycle); no more than 30% of the operating budget
deadline_text: 2025 cycle ran June 1 to July 15; 2026/2027 dates not posted, check site
requirements: 501(c)(3) located in or serving Greensboro and/or Guilford County
Focus areas: health and wellness, cultural vibrancy, economic mobility
No outstanding grant reports
notes: Guilford-focused; organizations serving uninsured people may also serve Randolph and Rockingham.

name: Sustaining Creativity: Community Partnerships Grant
amount_text: $10,000 to $25,000 tiered by budget (some awards reached $30,000 with bonuses); about $300,000 total
deadline_text: Annual; 2025-26 cycle closed Aug 15, 2025; check site for next cycle
requirements: Nonprofit with a primary focus on creative programming
Not already receiving significant City of Greensboro resources
Award tiers start at organizations with budgets of $20,000 to $100,000
notes: General operating support for arts nonprofits in Greensboro.

name: DGI Emergency Stabilization Fund
amount_text: Reimbursable grant up to $2,000
deadline_text: No deadline listed; check site
requirements: Small business located in downtown Greensboro
Covers repairs or cleaning after vandalism, graffiti, or other damage outside the owner's control
notes: Small reimbursement grant; DGI also has a $250 First Friday Activation Fund.

name: Kate B. Reynolds Charitable Trust Funding Opportunities
amount_text: Varies; recent Oct 2026 Forsyth grants ranged about $308,000 to $963,000
deadline_text: No open opportunities as of 2026-11-26; next not announced, check site
requirements: Review each opportunity's eligibility
Contact grants assistant for a phone consultation before applying
Forsyth focus areas: economic mobility, youth reconnection, safety net, two-generation support
notes: Major health funder; currently a watch-list item since all posted opportunities are closed.

name: Z. Smith Reynolds Foundation Community Progress Fund
amount_text: $20,000 to $40,000 per year for one or two years (max $80,000)
deadline_text: Annual; typically opens December and closes January or February; not currently accepting, check site
requirements: 501(c)(3), government, or religious entity in NC
Work must serve people in the applicant's community
Not eligible if funded by this program in the previous two years
notes: Winston-Salem-based funder; next cycle likely opens soon, so sign up for ZSR emails.

name: SBIR / STTR (America's Seed Fund)
funder: US Small Business Administration with 11 federal agencies
amount_text: Agency ceilings without SBA waiver: Phase I up to $335,937; Phase II up to $2,239,578 (as of Oct 16, 2026)
deadline_text: Rolling by agency solicitation; reauthorized through Sept 30, 2031
requirements: For-profit, US-based
Fewer than 500 employees
Owned and controlled by US citizens or permanent residents (VC ownership limits apply)
STTR requires a formal research institution partner
notes: The main federal R&D grant open to for-profits; pairs with NC One SBP Incentive and Matching funds.

name: USDA Rural Business Development Grants
amount_text: No maximum; smaller requests get priority; $27.7M national total in FY2026
deadline_text: Annual; FY2026 closed June 30, 2026 (SECD June 15); check site for FY2027
requirements: Public bodies, tribes, and nonprofits serving rural areas
For-profits and individuals are NOT eligible
Must benefit small and emerging rural businesses
Submit via Grants.gov by 4:30pm local time
notes: Funds the groups that help rural businesses (training, incubators, feasibility studies), not businesses directly.

name: USDA Rural Energy for America Program (REAP) Grants
amount_text: Grant amounts and cost share to be set in annual notice; per-entity annual cap applies (check site)
deadline_text: New final rule issued Oct 2026; application window to be announced in annual program notice
requirements: Agricultural producers and rural small businesses
Under new rule, projects must be fully built and operating before applying
Solar and wind on cropland are disincentivized
Single national competition
notes: Rules changed in Oct 2026; rural trucking or service businesses may qualify for efficiency upgrades.

name: USDA Value-Added Producer Grants
amount_text: Planning grants up to $50,000; working capital up to $200,000; 1:1 match required
deadline_text: Annual; FY2026 window Feb 17 to Apr 22, 2026 (closed); check site for FY2027
requirements: Agricultural producers, producer groups, farmer cooperatives, or majority producer-controlled ventures
Must produce and own more than half of the raw commodity
Dollar-for-dollar match (cash or in-kind)
notes: For farmers turning raw products into processed or branded goods.

name: EDA Public Works and Economic Adjustment Assistance
deadline_text: Rolling until a new NOFO is published or funds run out
requirements: Nonprofits, local and state governments, tribes, higher education
Individuals and for-profit entities are NOT eligible
Projects should align with a Comprehensive Economic Development Strategy (CEDS)
notes: Large infrastructure and planning grants; PTRC is the regional CEDS body to talk to.

name: SBA Program for Investment in Microentrepreneurs (PRIME)
deadline_text: Annual; FY2026 closed Aug 12, 2026; check Grants.gov for FY2027
requirements: Nonprofits (with or without 501(c)(3)), microenterprise development organizations, nonprofit CDFIs, tribal governments
Funds training and technical assistance for low-income microentrepreneurs
notes: For nonprofits that run small business training programs, not for the businesses themselves.

name: FMCSA Commercial Motor Vehicle Operator Safety Training (CMVOST) Grant
funder: US DOT Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration
amount_text: Up to $200,000; about $3.5M for about 25 awards in FY2026
deadline_text: Annual NOFO; FY2026 closed June 17, 2026; check site for FY2027
requirements: Accredited educational institutions, or non-accredited ones approved as DOL eligible training providers that accept WIOA and VA benefits
Government and education entities; nonprofits per Grants.gov listing
For-profit organizations and individuals are NOT eligible
Prioritizes training for veterans, Guard/Reserve, and military families
notes: Funds CDL schools training veterans; a carrier could partner with a community college applicant.

name: FMCSA High Priority Commercial Motor Vehicle (HP-CMV) Grant
funder: US DOT Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration
amount_text: Amount not stated on page (check NOFO)
deadline_text: Annual NOFO; check Grants.gov
requirements: State and local governments, tribes, higher education, 501(c)(3) nonprofits
For-profit organizations are NOT eligible
notes: Truck safety education and enforcement projects; not open to motor carriers directly.

name: Amber Grant
amount_text: Three $15,000 grants monthly (Monthly, Startup, Business Category); three $75,000 year-end grants to monthly winners
deadline_text: Monthly; each period closes 11:59pm ET on the last day of the month
requirements: Woman applicant age 18+
Business at least 50% women-owned
Based in US or Canada
Idea-stage and revenue-generating nonprofits allowed; charitable-giving nonprofits not allowed
$15 non-refundable application fee (hardship waiver available)
notes: Legit but has a $15 fee; one application can count for several monthly categories.

name: NASE Growth Grant
amount_text: Up to $4,000
deadline_text: Rolling; reviewed quarterly (Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct)
requirements: Must be an NASE member in good standing (Annual, Veteran, Gold immediately; Monthly after 90 days)
Uses: marketing, part-time hires, equipment, website, training, etc.
Cannot pay existing debt or rent/mortgage
notes: Requires paid NASE membership; good for solo operators needing equipment or marketing.

name: Freed Fellowship Grant
amount_text: $500 monthly to one Fellow; Fellows considered for an extra $2,500 at year-end
deadline_text: Rolling monthly; must be in by midnight ET on the last day of the month
requirements: Any US micro or small business owner
Nonprofits not supported
$19 application fee
notes: Small award with a $19 fee; one winner per month, so odds are long.

name: Hiring Our Heroes Small Business Grant Program
funder: U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation (Hiring Our Heroes), supported by FedEx
amount_text: Four $10,000 grants and one $25,000 grand prize
deadline_text: Due 11:59pm ET Dec 15, 2026; winners notified by Mar 29, 2027
requirements: At least 51% owned by a veteran (honorable discharge or current Guard/Reserve) or military spouse
For-profit with 3 to 20 workers including owner and 1099 contractors
Annual revenue under $5 million
In a distressed ZIP code (DCI score 40+) or able to show financial hardship
notes: Currently open; strong fit for veteran-owned small carriers that have a few drivers.

name: Tory Burch Foundation Fellows Program
amount_text: $2,000 education grant plus a year of coaching and advisors
deadline_text: Annual; 2027 cohort window was Sept 22 to Nov 17, 2026 (closed); fellows chosen May 2027
requirements: Woman 21+ who holds largest or equal-largest stake and a significant management role
Business at least 51% women-owned and controlled
Revenue of at least $75,000 a year
For-profit, US-formed and operating; legal US resident
notes: Mostly a fellowship; cash part is small. Watch for the September 2027 window.

name: Walmart Spark Good Local Grants
funder: Walmart Foundation / Walmart and Sam's Club stores
deadline_text: Three cycles a year (Feb 1 to Apr 15; May 1 to Jul 15; Aug 1 to Dec 31); page also lists a Nov 30 last day, so confirm
requirements: 501(c)(3) public charities, government entities, schools, or faith groups with community-wide projects
Must serve the same area as the requesting store
Verified Spark Good account on Walmart.com
One grant per facility per fiscal year
notes: Easy small grant for local nonprofits; apply to each nearby store separately.

name: Lowe's Hometowns Community Impact Grants
amount_text: About 100 large renovation grants from a $10M pool (one 2026 award was $200,000); per-grant range not stated
deadline_text: Annual nominations; 2026 window closed Mar 20, 2026; check site for 2027
requirements: Project must benefit a nonprofit, school, city, or municipality
Eligible: community centers, housing and shelters, parks, veteran services, first responder facilities, skilled trades facilities
notes: Big building renovation grants; nominations usually open in winter.

name: Foundation for a Healthy High Point Small Grants
funder: The Foundation for a Healthy High Point
region: Greater High Point, NC: High Point, Jamestown, Archdale, Trinity (Guilford, Randolph, Davidson, Forsyth counties)
amount_text: One-time awards up to $10,000; about $100,000 set aside per year
deadline_text: Rolling, year-round; decision within about one month
requirements: 501(c)(3), public agency, or group with a tax-exempt fiscal sponsor
Located in or largely serving Greater High Point, or expanding services there
Time-limited, non-renewable project
No for-profits or individuals
No past-due grant reports
notes: Rolling health and human services grants for Greater High Point nonprofits; needs audited financials and a staff/board roster.

name: Foundation for a Healthy High Point Impact Grants
funder: The Foundation for a Healthy High Point
region: Greater High Point, NC: High Point, Jamestown, Archdale, Trinity (Guilford, Randolph, Davidson, Forsyth counties)
amount_text: Requests over $10,000, no set maximum
deadline_text: Annual fall cycle: Fall 2026 LOIs were due Aug 13 and invited applications Oct 1, 2026; awards Dec 10 for grants starting Jan 1, 2027
requirements: 501(c)(3), public agency, or fiscally sponsored group
Located in or largely serving Greater High Point
2 to 3 page LOI first; full application by invitation
No medical research, transportation or housing services, direct client aid, or fundraisers
notes: Larger health grants for High Point nonprofits; starts with an LOI in summer.

name: Davie Community Foundation Community Grants
region: Davie County, NC (Mocksville, Cooleemee, Bermuda Run, Advance)
amount_text: No set range; 2026 awards ran $600 to $36,000
deadline_text: Twice a year: Feb 1 and Aug 1; next deadline Feb 1, 2027
requirements: Nonprofit programs serving Davie County (recipients have also included schools and the county parks department)
No annual fund drives, religious, or political activities
Apply through the online portal; annual grant report required
notes: Main open grant program for Davie County nonprofits; capacity-building requests are considered.

name: DGI First Friday Activation Fund
region: Greensboro, NC (Guilford County), Downtown Business Improvement District only
amount_text: Reimbursement up to $250 per First Friday event; can repeat for multiple events
deadline_text: Rolling, year-round; apply at least one week before the event
requirements: Physical storefront inside the downtown Greensboro BID
Fewer than 50 employees
Submit photos of the event and receipts after
notes: Tiny reimbursement for downtown storefronts that host First Friday activities.

name: Burlington Downtown Quick Fix Facade and Signage Grant
region: Burlington, NC (Alamance County), downtown Municipal Service District only
amount_text: 50/50 reimbursement up to $2,500 (project over $5,000 to get the max)
deadline_text: Rolling (other BDC small grants are quarterly: Jul 15, Oct 1, Jan 1, Apr 1)
requirements: Property or business owner inside the MSD (Webb Ave, Lexington Ave, Morehead St, Church St)
Exterior painting, windows, storefronts, awnings, signage
One grant per owner per year; cannot combine with other BDC grants
One-page application; no business plan required
notes: Fast facade/sign match for downtown Burlington; BDC's Up-Fit and Rehab programs are forgivable loans, not grants.

name: City of Graham Facade Grant Program
funder: City of Graham Historic Resources Commission and Planning Department
region: Graham, NC (Alamance County), Courthouse Square Historic District only
amount_text: 50/50 reimbursement, up to $5,000 per property per year
deadline_text: Annual; 2026-27 packets were due Oct 23, 2026 (COA due Sept 25); work done by May 1, 2027
requirements: Owner or tenant of a non-residential building in the district (tenants need owner letter)
Exterior work only, approved by the HRC before work starts
Two itemized cost estimates
Paid receipts and city inspection before reimbursement
notes: Yearly facade match for downtown Graham; next round likely opens late summer 2027.

name: Town of Elkin Downtown Facade Grant
funder: Town of Elkin Main Street Advisory Board
region: Elkin, NC (Surry County), downtown Municipal Service District only
amount_text: 50/50 match up to $1,500 per building; $5,000 total pool for FY2026-27
deadline_text: Annual fiscal-year cycle; FY2026-27 applications by February 2027 (no exact day posted), reimbursement paperwork by May
requirements: Downtown building owner in the MSD
Work by an insured contractor; no DIY reimbursement
Approval before work begins
Must meet historic preservation standards
notes: Small facade match for downtown Elkin; the town also offers free design help.

name: Downtown Thomasville Facade Grant and Window Facade Grant
funder: The PACE Group Inc. (Downtown Thomasville revitalization)
region: Thomasville, NC (Davidson County), Downtown Business Improvement District only
amount_text: Amount not posted on the page; see program guidelines PDF
deadline_text: Rolling as funds allow until spent (2025 round listed as open)
requirements: Owner or tenant of a building in the Thomasville Downtown BID
Check the district map first
notes: Downtown Thomasville facade money; amount and current funding not confirmed, call before applying.

name: Guilford County Community-Based Organization Funding
amount_text: FY2026 awards ranged $3,000 to $75,000; typical $25,000 to $50,000
deadline_text: Annual; FY2027 window was Sept 4 to Oct 5, 2026 (closed); board approves allocations in December
requirements: Registered, active 501(c) with an office in or mostly serving Guilford County
Certificate of liability insurance naming Guilford County
Board roster; audit if requesting over $100,000
After award: notarized no-overdue-taxes, conflict of interest policy, E-Verify affidavit; quarterly reports
notes: County general-fund grants to nonprofits; one-session online form, so prepare attachments first.

name: Cone Health Community Grant Requests
region: Cone Health service area: Greensboro and Guilford, Alamance, Rockingham counties, NC (page lists no counties)
amount_text: No amounts published
deadline_text: Twice a year: submit by April 24 or October 25 (page shows no year); reviewed in June and November
requirements: 501(c)(3) with a record of financial stewardship
Fits a Cone Health giving value: prevention, access, patient outcomes, or support in hard times
One application per organization per calendar year
Not for individual schools, youth sports, scouting, churches, or political groups
notes: Health system community grants; 990 on request and numbered invoice needed for payment. Service area inferred from hospital locations; confirm with the funder.

name: United Way of Greater Greensboro Community Impact and Bold Goal Grants
amount_text: Amounts not stated in the announcement
deadline_text: 2026-27 cycle opened Dec 2025 with required Grant Seeker Meetings Dec 16 and 17; check site for the next cycle
requirements: Local nonprofit
Must attend a Grant Seeker Meeting before applying
Programs in youth opportunity, financial security, or healthy communities; Bold Goal track is for raising family income above poverty
notes: Multi-year style partner grants; the full guidelines page did not load, so deadlines are unconfirmed.

name: Artist Support Grants (Davidson, Davie, Forsyth, Guilford, Randolph consortium)
funder: NC Arts Council, administered by Arts Council of Winston-Salem and Forsyth County and ArtsGreensboro
region: Davidson, Davie, Forsyth, Guilford, Randolph counties, NC
deadline_text: Annual; 2026 round opened June 1 and closed Sept 4, 2026
requirements: Individual artist or unincorporated artist collective living in one of the five counties
Spends a significant part of time on art work
For new work, equipment, business operations, training, or reaching new audiences
notes: For working artists only; apply through intothearts.org (Davidson, Davie, Forsyth) or theacgg.org (Guilford, Randolph).

name: NC Arts Council Project Support Grants
funder: North Carolina Arts Council (NC Dept. of Natural and Cultural Resources)
amount_text: $5,000 to $15,000 ($5,000 cap if prior-year expenses $20K to $50K)
deadline_text: Annual; FY2026-27 applications ran Jan 5 to Mar 2, 2026 for projects July 2026 to June 2027
requirements: NC 501(c)(3) with at least 2 years of arts programming
Prior-year cash operating expenses of at least $20,000, or apply through a fiscal agent
One-third cash match in Tier 2 and 3 counties; waived in Tier 1
EIN and UEI in the OPAL grant portal
notes: State arts project grants; a UEI is needed even though this is a state program.

name: NC Agricultural Development and Farmland Preservation Trust Fund Grants
funder: NC Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, Farmland Preservation Division
amount_text: Varies by project; $51.2 million awarded statewide in Oct 2026
deadline_text: Annual cycle; Cycle 20 Part 2 closes Dec 21, 2026 for non-easement projects, but Part 1 closed Aug 31, 2026, so new applicants wait for the next cycle
requirements: Applicant must be a county or a nonprofit conservation organization
Farmers and landowners take part only through such a partner
Projects: conservation easements, agricultural development projects, agricultural plans, growth zones
notes: Farm-sector grants that flow through counties and land trusts; a farm business needs a county or nonprofit partner.

name: NC State Energy Program Energy Efficiency Subgrant
funder: NC Department of Environmental Quality, State Energy Office (US DOE State Energy Program funds)
amount_text: $50,000 to $200,000 per project; about $1.4 million total
deadline_text: 2026 RFP ran Oct 22 to Nov 24, 2026 (closed); awards expected early 2027
requirements: Energy-efficiency building upgrades (audits optional)
Project finished by June 30, 2027
Priority to applicants with a prior energy audit
Federal rules may apply (NEPA, historic review)
notes: Open to businesses, but sized for building upgrades of $50K or more; watch for a 2027 RFP.

name: Golden LEAF Economic Catalyst
region: North Carolina (tobacco-dependent or economically distressed areas)
amount_text: No cap published; sized to jobs, distress, and impact
deadline_text: Rolling; board reviews at the next meeting at least six weeks after a complete proposal
requirements: Applicant is a government or 501(c)(3) on behalf of a specific job-creating company
Company commits to full-time jobs (1,600+ hours/yr) that are at risk without the grant
Company pays at least half of employee-only health insurance
Must apply before the company announces its NC location decision
notes: Recruitment/expansion money a growing company can ask its county EDC to pursue; pro rata repayment if jobs fall short.

name: NC Rural Infrastructure Grant
funder: NC Department of Commerce, Rural Economic Development Division / Rural Infrastructure Authority
region: North Carolina (Tier 1 and 2 counties, rural census tracts in Tier 3)
amount_text: Set per project based on jobs and impact; 5% cash match
deadline_text: Several rounds a year; next deadline Feb 22, 2027 (awards Apr 15, 2027)
requirements: Local government applies
Tied to new full-time private-sector jobs
5% cash match, not from other state or federal grants
Repay if jobs are not created and kept six months
notes: Water, sewer or road money a town can seek for a business that is adding jobs; Guilford and Forsyth only qualify in rural tracts.

name: NC Rural Downtown Economic Development Grant
funder: NC Department of Commerce, NC Main Street and Rural Planning Center / Rural Infrastructure Authority
amount_text: Amount not published; 5% local match
deadline_text: Three rounds a year; next deadline Jan 7, 2027, then Apr 29, 2027
requirements: Local government applies
Public infrastructure, publicly owned buildings, or mixed-use on public property downtown
Job creation/retention projection and environmental review
notes: Downtown public improvements; a business benefits indirectly through its town.

name: NCEdge Customized Training Program
funder: NC Community College System with local community colleges (listed by NC Commerce)
amount_text: No-cost training designed and delivered by the local community college
deadline_text: Ongoing; contact your local community college
requirements: Industry: manufacturing, IT, life sciences, logistics or warehousing, customer support centers, air courier, or regional/national HQ
Meet two of: capital investment, new jobs, new technology, workforce expansion, productivity gains, skill upgrades
notes: Free employer training; local trucking is not a listed industry, but logistics and warehousing are.

name: Duke Energy Foundation Small Business Impact Program (NC microgrants via local nonprofits)
region: North Carolina (communities served by Duke Energy)
amount_text: Nonprofits get up to $25,000; they pass on Impact Awards up to $5,000 to small businesses with 50 or fewer workers
deadline_text: Annual since 2020; 2026 nonprofit deadline June 30, 2026; businesses apply to the funded local nonprofit when it opens its microgrants
requirements: Nonprofit applicant: 501(c)(3) serving Duke Energy communities
Business award: 50 or fewer employees
Business uses: renovations, equipment, technology, inventory; not payroll, rent, or utilities
notes: A for-profit cannot apply to Duke directly; watch local chambers and downtown groups for the microgrant round.

name: Verizon Small Business Digital Ready $10K Grants
amount_text: $10,000; 10 businesses picked each month
deadline_text: Monthly reviews June to December 2026; finish two free courses or events by Dec 7, 2026 to unlock the one application; decisions by Jan 12, 2027
requirements: Owner 18+ of a US for-profit small business
Register on Digital Ready and complete any two eligible courses or events
One application per owner; no nonprofits
Finalists verify tax and bank info
notes: Low-effort national grant; applications filed before Apr 15, 2026 had to be redone.

name: Allstate Main Street Grants Program
funder: Allstate with Hello Alice and Global Entrepreneurship Network
amount_text: $20,000 to 100 of up to 250 Boost Camp participants ($2 million total)
deadline_text: 2026 round closed June 23, 2026; grant recipients announced Nov 28, 2026
requirements: For-profit registered in a US state, DC, or Puerto Rico
At least $25,000 revenue in 2025
Applicant is the lead executive, 18+
Join a 12-week virtual Boost Camp; acceptance does not guarantee a grant
notes: Closed for 2026; listed so it can be watched for a 2027 round.

name: Pilot Small Business Growth Fund
amount_text: 18 grants: one $50,000, two $25,000, fifteen $10,000, plus a year of Pilot bookkeeping
deadline_text: 2026 round ran Feb 24 to Mar 31, 2026 (closed)
requirements: For-profit registered and located in a US state, DC, or Puerto Rico
2025 gross revenue between $5,000 and $5,000,000
Applicant is the lead executive, 18+
Finalists may submit a short video
notes: Closed for 2026; listed so it can be watched for a 2027 round.
